usage: Fiscal and accounting verb: to deduct an amount from a sum, above all from taxes ('detrarre le spese mediche', 'detrazione fiscale'); technically distinct from 'dedurre' (deduct from taxable income) in Italian tax law. Irregular like 'trarre': detraggo, detrassi, detratto, detrarrò.

examples.it: Puoi detrarre il 19 per cento delle spese sanitarie.
examples.en: You can deduct 19 percent of your medical expenses.

examples.it: Dall'importo vanno detratte le somme già versate.
examples.en: The sums already paid must be deducted from the amount.

examples.it: Detrassero dallo stipendio i giorni di assenza ingiustificata.
examples.en: They deducted the days of unjustified absence from his salary.

en: to tear to pieces, to rend; to torment
usage: Literary and journalistic: literally of wild beasts tearing flesh, figuratively of grief, remorse or factional strife ('un partito dilaniato dalle correnti'). Stronger than 'lacerare' and 'straziare'; the pronominal 'dilaniarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to tear one another apart. Regular -are verb (dilanio, dilani).

examples.it: Le belve dilaniarono la carcassa in pochi minuti.
examples.en: The beasts tore the carcass to pieces in a few minutes.

examples.it: Il rimorso lo dilaniava giorno e notte.
examples.en: Remorse tormented him day and night.

examples.it: Il paese è dilaniato da una guerra civile che dura da anni.
examples.en: The country is torn apart by a civil war that has been going on for years.

en: to vanish, to melt away; to slip away
usage: Elegant verb for disappearing gradually or unnoticed: mist, sounds, hopes and, colloquially, people who slip away without paying ('si è dileguato con la cassa'). Compare 'svanire' (to fade) and 'sparire' (neutral, sudden). Regular -are verb; the transitive 'dileguare' is literary.

examples.it: La nebbia si dileguò con i primi raggi del sole.
examples.en: The mist melted away with the first rays of the sun.

examples.it: I ladri si sono dileguati prima dell'arrivo della polizia.
examples.en: The thieves vanished before the police arrived.

examples.it: Ogni speranza si dileguerebbe, se lui non tornasse.
examples.en: All hope would vanish, if he did not return.

en: to wag, to wave about, to shake; (dimenarsi) to thrash about, to wriggle
usage: To move part of the body back and forth with energy: a dog 'dimena la coda', a dancer 'dimena i fianchi'; the pronominal 'dimenarsi' (auxiliary essere) is to thrash about, also figuratively to struggle ('dimenarsi tra mille impegni'). Colloquial-descriptive; 'agitare' is the neutral verb. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il cane dimenava la coda festoso.
examples.en: The dog was wagging its tail joyfully.

examples.it: Il pesce si dimenò sulla banchina finché non lo ributtarono in acqua.
examples.en: The fish thrashed about on the pier until they threw it back into the water.

examples.it: Smetti di dimenarti e stai fermo mentre ti pettino.
examples.en: Stop wriggling and keep still while I comb your hair.

en: to unravel, to disentangle; to sort out (a problem)
usage: From winding yarn off a skein: to disentangle an intricate matter ('dipanare la matassa', to sort out the tangle). The pronominal 'dipanarsi' (auxiliary essere) describes a plot or a road unfolding. More literary than 'sbrogliare' and 'districare'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ci vorranno mesi per dipanare l'intreccio di società offshore.
examples.en: It will take months to unravel the web of offshore companies.

examples.it: La trama si dipana lentamente, tra flashback e digressioni.
examples.en: The plot unfolds slowly, between flashbacks and digressions.

examples.it: Se avessimo dipanato subito il malinteso, non saremmo qui a litigare.
examples.en: If we had cleared up the misunderstanding right away, we wouldn't be here arguing.

en: to discern; to distinguish; to tell apart
usage: Literary-philosophical for perceiving fine distinctions ('discernere il vero dal falso'); the noun 'discernimento' is the faculty of judgement. Defective: it lacks a past participle in modern use ('discreto' is now only an adjective), so compound tenses are avoided in favour of 'distinguere'.

examples.it: A quell'età i bambini non discernono ancora la fantasia dalla realtà.
examples.en: At that age children do not yet distinguish fantasy from reality.

examples.it: Nella nebbia si discerneva a stento la sagoma del faro.
examples.en: In the fog one could barely make out the outline of the lighthouse.

examples.it: Ci vorrà saggezza per discernere ciò che conta davvero.
examples.en: It will take wisdom to discern what really matters.

en: to disown; to refuse to acknowledge; to deny (paternity, merit)
usage: Juridical in 'disconoscere un figlio / la paternità' (to deny paternity) and formal for refusing to recognise a merit, authority or obligation ('non si possono disconoscere i suoi meriti'). Irregular like conoscere: disconobbi, disconosciuto.

examples.it: Nessuno può disconoscere il contributo che ha dato alla scienza.
examples.en: No one can deny the contribution he made to science.

examples.it: L'uomo disconobbe il figlio davanti al giudice.
examples.en: The man denied paternity of the child before the judge.

examples.it: La minoranza ha disconosciuto l'esito del voto.
examples.en: The minority refused to recognise the result of the vote.

en: to discourse at length (learnedly or pedantically)
usage: To discuss a subject in a learned, subtle and often pedantic way ('disquisire di massimi sistemi'); the noun 'disquisizione' is frequently ironic ('lunghe disquisizioni filosofiche'). Conjugated with -isc- (disquisisco); governs 'di', 'su' or 'intorno a'.

examples.it: Disquisirono per ore sul sesso degli angeli mentre la casa bruciava.
examples.en: They discoursed for hours on the sex of angels while the house burned.

examples.it: Non è il momento di disquisire di filosofia del diritto.
examples.en: This is not the time to hold forth on the philosophy of law.

examples.it: Che disquisisca pure di etica: i fatti parlano da soli.
examples.en: Let him hold forth on ethics: the facts speak for themselves.

en: to break up (uncultivated ground), to till for the first time; to clear (land)
usage: Agricultural term for turning over hard, uncultivated soil to make it arable; figuratively, to prepare the ground for a new field of study ('dissodare un terreno di ricerca'). 'Arare' is routine ploughing, 'dissodare' the first, hard breaking of the sod. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: I coloni dissodarono la brughiera e vi piantarono grano.
examples.en: The settlers broke up the heath and planted wheat there.

examples.it: Bisognerà dissodare il campo prima che arrivino le piogge.
examples.en: The field will have to be broken up before the rains come.

examples.it: Quei primi studiosi hanno dissodato un terreno che altri avrebbero coltivato.
examples.en: Those first scholars broke ground that others would go on to cultivate.

en: to diverge; to differ; to branch apart
usage: Scientific for lines or paths moving apart and formal for opinions differing ('le posizioni divergono su un punto'); the opposite of 'convergere'. Defective: it has no past participle and hence no compound tenses (use 'differire' or 'essere diversi'); the rare passato remoto is diversi, divergesti.

examples.it: Le nostre opinioni divergono solo sui dettagli.
examples.en: Our opinions differ only in the details.

examples.it: Da quel punto i due sentieri divergevano nettamente.
examples.en: From that point the two paths branched sharply apart.

examples.it: È inevitabile che le strategie dei due partiti divergano.
examples.en: It is inevitable that the two parties' strategies should diverge.

en: to complain; to regret; to grieve (literary)
usage: Literary and juridical ('la parte si duole della decisione' in appeal briefs) for expressing regret or complaint. Highly irregular: mi dolgo, ti duoli, si duole, ci doliamo, vi dolete, si dolgono; mi dolsi; dolutosi; future mi dorrò; subjunctive mi dolga. Everyday Italian uses 'lamentarsi' or 'dispiacersi'.

examples.it: Il ricorrente si duole della mancata audizione dei testimoni.
examples.en: The appellant complains that the witnesses were not heard.

examples.it: Mi dolgo di non averlo ascoltato quando era ancora in tempo.
examples.en: I regret not having listened to him while there was still time.

examples.it: Si dolse a lungo con l'amico per l'offesa ricevuta.
examples.en: He complained at length to his friend about the offence he had suffered.

en: to sweeten; to water down, to sugar-coat
usage: Literally a pharmaceutical term (to add sweetener), almost always figurative today: to soften a harsh truth or an account ('una versione edulcorata dei fatti'). Journalistic-critical register; 'addolcire' is neutral, 'edulcorare' implies disapproval of the concealment. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il film edulcora la biografia del protagonista fino a renderla irriconoscibile.
examples.en: The film sugar-coats the protagonist's life story to the point of making it unrecognisable.

examples.it: Non edulcorate la diagnosi: vogliamo sapere la verità.
examples.en: Don't water down the diagnosis: we want to know the truth.

examples.it: Ci hanno raccontato una storia edulcorata, ma la realtà era ben più cruda.
examples.en: They told us a sanitised story, but the reality was far harsher.

en: to pour out, to give vent to (feelings); (effondersi) to spread, to overflow
usage: Aulic Latinism for pouring out feelings, light or fragrance; today survives mainly in the pronominal 'effondersi in' (to launch into effusive expressions: 'effondersi in ringraziamenti', auxiliary essere) and in the noun 'effusione'. Irregular like 'fondere': effusi, effuso.

examples.it: Il poeta effondeva nei versi tutto il suo dolore.
examples.en: The poet poured all his grief into his verses.

examples.it: Si effuse in lodi sperticate verso il nuovo direttore.
examples.en: He launched into extravagant praise of the new director.

examples.it: Un profumo di gelsomino si era effuso per tutto il giardino.
examples.en: A scent of jasmine had spread throughout the garden.

en: to bestow generously; to lavish; to grant
usage: Formal verb for giving generously from a position of abundance or power ('elargire contributi, premi, favori'); often ironic when applied to advice or promises ('elargire consigli non richiesti'). 'Donare' is neutral, 'dispensare' more mechanical. Conjugated with -isc- (elargisco).

examples.it: La fondazione elargisce ogni anno borse di studio a studenti meritevoli.
examples.en: Every year the foundation awards scholarships to deserving students.

examples.it: Il sovrano elargì titoli e terre ai suoi fedeli.
examples.en: The sovereign bestowed titles and lands on his loyal followers.

examples.it: Vorrei che smettesse di elargire consigli che nessuno gli ha chiesto.
examples.en: I wish he would stop dispensing advice nobody asked him for.

en: to cogitate laboriously; to concoct (theories) by long brooding
usage: Learned and mostly ironic (from 'lucubrare', to work by lamplight): to produce ideas through long and tortuous mental effort; the noun 'elucubrazione' is almost always spregiativo ('le sue elucubrazioni'). Regular -are verb (elùcubro).

examples.it: Passò la notte a elucubrare un piano per riconquistarla.
examples.en: He spent the night cogitating a plan to win her back.

examples.it: Invece di elucubrare teorie, prova a parlare con lei.
examples.en: Instead of concocting theories, try talking to her.

examples.it: Cosa avrà elucubrato questa volta la nostra commissione?
examples.en: What will our committee have dreamt up this time?

en: to amend (a law, a text); to correct; (emendarsi) to mend one's ways
usage: Parliamentary and philological verb: to amend a bill ('emendare un disegno di legge') or to correct a corrupt text; the moral sense 'emendarsi' (auxiliary essere) is literary. The noun 'emendamento' is everyday political vocabulary. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La commissione ha emendato l'articolo 5 in più punti.
examples.en: The committee amended Article 5 in several places.

examples.it: Il filologo emendò il passo corrotto ricorrendo a un manoscritto più antico.
examples.en: The philologist corrected the corrupt passage by resorting to an older manuscript.

examples.it: Chi si emenda dei propri errori merita una seconda possibilità.
examples.en: Whoever mends their ways deserves a second chance.

en: to rise up; to tower; (ergersi a) to set oneself up as
usage: Literary for buildings or mountains towering over a landscape ('la torre si erge sulla piana'), and figurative-critical in 'ergersi a giudice / paladino / difensore' (to set oneself up as). Irregular: mi ergo, si erge; passato remoto si erse; participle erto; the transitive 'ergere' (to raise) is archaic.

examples.it: Il campanile si erge solitario sopra i tetti del borgo.
examples.en: The bell tower rises alone above the roofs of the village.

examples.it: Nessuno gli ha dato il diritto di ergersi a giudice degli altri.
examples.en: No one gave him the right to set himself up as a judge of others.

examples.it: Sulla collina si ergeva un castello in rovina.
examples.en: On the hill stood a ruined castle.

en: to burst out, to erupt; to break out (into laughter, tears)
usage: Literary verb for a sudden violent outburst: lava from a volcano, water from a breach, a cry or laughter from a person ('erompere in singhiozzi'). 'Prorompere' is the closer synonym, 'scoppiare' the everyday one. Irregular like 'rompere': eruppe, erotto (participle rare); auxiliary essere.

examples.it: Dalla folla eruppe un grido di gioia.
examples.en: A cry of joy burst from the crowd.

examples.it: La lava erompeva dal cratere illuminando la notte.
examples.en: Lava was erupting from the crater, lighting up the night.

examples.it: Temevo che erompesse in lacrime davanti a tutti.
examples.en: I feared she would burst into tears in front of everyone.

en: to exacerbate; to embitter; to aggravate
usage: Learned verb for making a conflict, a pain or a mood harsher ('esacerbare gli animi', 'esacerbare le tensioni'); the pronominal 'esacerbarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to become embittered or worse. Compare 'inasprire' (neutral-formal) and 'acuire'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Le dichiarazioni del ministro hanno esacerbato gli animi.
examples.en: The minister's statements inflamed people's feelings.

examples.it: Il dolore si esacerbò durante la notte.
examples.en: The pain grew worse during the night.

examples.it: Temo che una nuova tassa esacerbi il malcontento popolare.
examples.en: I fear that a new tax will exacerbate popular discontent.

en: to execrate, to loathe; to condemn with horror
usage: Solemn, almost religious verb for detesting and cursing something as abominable; used in high moral and political prose ('un crimine esecrato da tutti'). Stronger than 'detestare' and 'aborrire'. Regular -are verb: 'esècro' (stress on the second e); the adjective 'esecrabile' is more common than the verb.

examples.it: Tutti esecrano quel massacro, ma pochi ne parlano.
examples.en: Everyone abhors that massacre, but few speak of it.

examples.it: I contemporanei esecrarono il tiranno che i posteri avrebbero riabilitato.
examples.en: His contemporaries execrated the tyrant whom posterity would rehabilitate.

examples.it: Non basta che si esecri la violenza a parole.
examples.en: It is not enough to condemn violence in words.

en: to expunge, to delete (from a text or list)
patterns: espungere un passo da un testo
usage: Philological and juridical verb: to remove a word, passage or clause considered spurious or inadmissible ('espungere una clausola dal contratto'). Everyday speech says 'togliere' or 'cancellare'; 'depennare' is its bureaucratic cousin. Irregular like 'pungere': espunsi, espunto.

examples.it: L'editore espunse dal testo le interpolazioni più evidenti.
examples.en: The editor expunged the most obvious interpolations from the text.

examples.it: Il giudice ha espunto dal fascicolo le intercettazioni irrilevanti.
examples.en: The judge removed the irrelevant wiretaps from the case file.

examples.it: Vorrei che quel paragrafo fosse espunto dalla versione definitiva.
examples.en: I would like that paragraph to be deleted from the final version.

en: to extort; to wring (a confession, a promise) out of someone
usage: Juridical and journalistic: to obtain money or a statement by threat, violence or pressure ('estorcere una confessione con la tortura'); the crime is 'estorsione'. Irregular like 'torcere': estorsi, estorto. Note the indirect object with 'a' for the victim.

examples.it: La banda estorceva denaro ai commercianti del quartiere.
examples.en: The gang extorted money from the neighbourhood shopkeepers.

examples.it: Gli estorsero una confessione dopo dodici ore di interrogatorio.
examples.en: They wrung a confession out of him after twelve hours of questioning.

examples.it: Una promessa estorta con il ricatto non vale nulla.
examples.en: A promise extorted by blackmail is worth nothing.

en: to express outwardly, to manifest; (estrinsecarsi) to take concrete form
usage: Philosophical and bureaucratic Latinism: to bring an inner quality or intention into external form ('estrinsecare il proprio pensiero'); the pronominal 'estrinsecarsi in' (auxiliary essere) is common in official prose ('l'attività si estrinseca in tre fasi'). 'Manifestare' or 'esprimere' are the plain alternatives. Regular -are verb (estrinsechi).

examples.it: La sua ostilità si estrinsecava in piccoli dispetti quotidiani.
examples.en: His hostility manifested itself in small daily spites.

examples.it: L'artista estrinsecò nel colore ciò che non riusciva a dire a parole.
examples.en: The artist expressed in colour what he could not say in words.

examples.it: Vorremmo che il vostro impegno si estrinsecasse in atti concreti.
examples.en: We would like your commitment to take the form of concrete acts.

en: to rave; to talk deliriously, to talk nonsense
usage: Literally to be delirious with fever; figuratively, and strongly spregiativo, to spout absurd ideas ('farnetica di complotti'). 'Delirare' is medical or emphatic, 'vaneggiare' more literary, 'farneticare' the harsher everyday judgement. Regular -are verb (farnetichi); the noun is 'farneticazione'.

examples.it: Il malato farneticava e chiamava persone morte da anni.
examples.en: The patient was raving and calling out to people long dead.

examples.it: Che cosa farnetichi? Nessuno vuole licenziarti.
examples.en: What are you raving about? Nobody wants to fire you.

examples.it: Chiunque lo ascolti per cinque minuti capisce che farnetica.
examples.en: Anyone who listens to him for five minutes realises he's talking nonsense.

en: to come to terms with (farsene una ragione); to do (something) with (che me ne faccio?)
patterns: non sapere che farsene di qualcosa
usage: Pronominal idiom with fixed 'se ne': 'farsene una ragione' means to accept something painful ('me ne sono fatto una ragione'); 'che me ne faccio?' means 'what am I supposed to do with it?', and 'non saper che farsene di' means to have no use for. Irregular like fare: me ne faccio, se ne fece, se ne è fatto; the participle agrees with the subject or with the object 'ragione' ('se ne è fatta una ragione').

examples.it: È finita, e prima o poi dovrai fartene una ragione.
examples.en: It's over, and sooner or later you will have to come to terms with it.

examples.it: Che me ne faccio di un altro caricabatterie?
examples.en: What am I supposed to do with another charger?

examples.it: Se ne fece una ragione solo dopo molti anni.
examples.en: He came to terms with it only after many years.

en: to cleave, to split; to cut through (water, a crowd)
usage: Literary verb for splitting with a sharp blow or cutting through a medium: 'fendere l'aria', 'la prua fende le onde', 'un grido fendette il silenzio'. The pronominal 'fendersi' means to crack open. Passato remoto 'fendei' or 'fendetti'; the participle is 'fenduto', with the archaic 'fesso' surviving only as an adjective (also colloquially 'fool').

examples.it: La nave fendeva le onde a tutta velocità.
examples.en: The ship was cutting through the waves at full speed.

examples.it: Un urlo fendette il silenzio della notte.
examples.en: A scream rent the silence of the night.

examples.it: Il terremoto ha fenduto la parete della chiesa dal tetto al pavimento.
examples.en: The earthquake has split the church wall from roof to floor.

en: to fund, to bankroll (often covertly); to supply with fodder
usage: From 'foraggio' (fodder): originally to feed horses, today almost always journalistic and spregiativo for financing a party, newspaper or clientele to buy its loyalty ('foraggiare la stampa amica'). 'Finanziare' is neutral, 'sovvenzionare' formal. Regular -are verb (foraggio, foraggi).

examples.it: Per anni il regime ha foraggiato i giornali compiacenti.
examples.en: For years the regime bankrolled the compliant newspapers.

examples.it: Si sospetta che quella fondazione foraggi gruppi estremisti.
examples.en: That foundation is suspected of funding extremist groups.

examples.it: Chi avrà foraggiato una campagna elettorale così costosa?
examples.en: Who can have bankrolled such an expensive election campaign?

en: to break, to shatter; (frangersi) to break (of waves)
usage: Literary verb (Dante, Leopardi) that in modern Italian survives chiefly in the pronominal 'frangersi' for waves breaking on rocks (auxiliary essere) and in derivatives ('frangiflutti', 'infrangere', 'frantoio'). Irregular: fransi, franto; the transitive sense also covers crushing olives.

examples.it: Le onde si frangevano con fragore contro la scogliera.
examples.en: The waves were breaking noisily against the cliff.

examples.it: Nel frantoio le olive vengono frante entro poche ore dalla raccolta.
examples.en: In the mill the olives are crushed within a few hours of harvesting.

examples.it: Ogni sua speranza si franse contro l'indifferenza dei giudici.
examples.en: All his hopes were shattered against the indifference of the judges.

en: to interpose; to put (obstacles, delays) in the way; (frapporsi) to come between
usage: Formal, chiefly in 'frapporre ostacoli' (to put obstacles in the way) and 'senza frapporre indugi' (without delay); the pronominal 'frapporsi' (aux essere) means to come between two parties or things. Irregular like porre: frappongo, frapposi, frapposto; future frapporrò.

examples.it: La burocrazia frappone ostacoli a ogni iniziativa privata.
examples.en: Bureaucracy puts obstacles in the way of every private initiative.

examples.it: Il governo agì senza frapporre indugi.
examples.en: The government acted without delay.

examples.it: Non voglio che nessuno si frapponga tra me e mia figlia.
examples.en: I don't want anyone to come between me and my daughter.

en: to chirp, to twitter (of swallows); to flutter (of flags)
usage: Poetic verb (Pascoli, D'Annunzio) for the shrill cry of swallows and, by extension, for banners snapping in the wind ('bandiere che garriscono al vento'). Conjugated with -isc- (garrisce); used almost only in the third person. 'Cinguettare' is the everyday verb for birdsong.

examples.it: Le rondini garrivano intorno al campanile.
examples.en: The swallows were twittering around the bell tower.

examples.it: Sulla torre garriva la bandiera della repubblica.
examples.en: On the tower the flag of the republic fluttered in the wind.

examples.it: Che le rondini garriscano ancora sotto quel tetto è un buon segno.
examples.en: That swallows still chirp under that roof is a good sign.

en: to seize with claws, to snatch; to grab suddenly
usage: Literary verb for a bird of prey or beast seizing its victim, extended to sudden violent grabbing by people or by death and illness ('la morte lo ghermì nel sonno'). Conjugated with -isc- (ghermisco); 'afferrare' is the neutral equivalent, 'artigliare' the closest synonym.

examples.it: Il falco ghermì la lepre e si alzò in volo.
examples.en: The hawk seized the hare and rose into the air.

examples.it: Una mano lo ghermì per il colletto e lo trascinò indietro.
examples.en: A hand grabbed him by the collar and dragged him back.

examples.it: Temo che la febbre lo abbia ghermito proprio alla vigilia della partenza.
examples.en: I fear the fever seized him right on the eve of his departure.

en: to juxtapose; to place side by side (without linking)
usage: Critical-academic verb for setting two elements next to each other without blending them ('il regista giustappone immagini di guerra e di festa'); the noun is 'giustapposizione'. Irregular like porre: giustappongo, giustapposi, giustapposto; future giustapporrò.

examples.it: L'autore giustappone episodi comici e tragici senza transizione.
examples.en: The author juxtaposes comic and tragic episodes without any transition.

examples.it: Nel collage ha giustapposto ritagli di giornale e fotografie di famiglia.
examples.en: In the collage she placed newspaper cuttings side by side with family photographs.

examples.it: Se giustapponessimo i due grafici, le differenze salterebbero agli occhi.
examples.en: If we set the two charts side by side, the differences would leap out.

en: to gloat; to be overjoyed, to beam with satisfaction
usage: Familiar and picturesque: to show open, slightly smug delight ('gongolava per la promozione'), often with the undertone of gloating over a rival's misfortune. 'Esultare' is the neutral verb for rejoicing; 'gongolare' adds the visible glow of self-satisfaction. Regular -are verb (góngolo).

examples.it: Gongolava come un bambino davanti ai complimenti.
examples.en: He was beaming like a child at the compliments.

examples.it: I tifosi gongolarono per tutta la settimana dopo il derby.
examples.en: The fans gloated all week after the derby.

examples.it: Non gongolare troppo: la rivincita è tra un mese.
examples.en: Don't gloat too much: the rematch is in a month.

en: to fill to overflowing, to pack; (gremirsi) to fill up (with people)
usage: Journalistic-literary verb for crowds filling a place completely ('una folla gremiva la piazza'); the participle 'gremito' ('teatro gremito in ogni ordine di posti') is the most common form, and 'gremirsi' (auxiliary essere) means to fill up. Conjugated with -isc- (gremisce). 'Riempire' is neutral; 'affollare' close but less intense.

examples.it: Una folla immensa gremiva la basilica.
examples.en: An immense crowd packed the basilica.

examples.it: Lo stadio si gremì un'ora prima del fischio d'inizio.
examples.en: The stadium filled up an hour before kick-off.

examples.it: Spero che la sala si gremisca anche per la replica.
examples.en: I hope the hall will be packed for the second performance too.

en: to hawk, to tout; to win over with glib talk
usage: From the street-market 'imbonitore' (barker): to attract and soften up an audience or a customer with a torrent of persuasive patter; spregiativo when applied to politicians or salesmen. Conjugated with -isc- (imbonisco). 'Lusingare' flatters, 'imbonire' sells.

examples.it: Il venditore imboniva i passanti con promesse mirabolanti.
examples.en: The seller was hawking to passers-by with amazing promises.

examples.it: Non farti imbonire da chi promette rendimenti garantiti.
examples.en: Don't let yourself be sweet-talked by anyone promising guaranteed returns.

examples.it: Imbonì la platea per venti minuti prima di arrivare al dunque.
examples.en: He softened up the audience for twenty minutes before getting to the point.

en: to fatten; to swell (coffers, a bank account); (impinguarsi) to grow fat, to enrich oneself
usage: From 'pingue' (fat): literally to fatten animals, figuratively and often ironically to swell coffers, files or bank accounts ('impinguare il bilancio con nuove tasse'). The pronominal 'impinguarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to get fat or rich at others' expense. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Le multe servivano solo a impinguare le casse del comune.
examples.en: The fines served only to swell the municipality's coffers.

examples.it: Qualcuno si è impinguato con i fondi destinati alla ricostruzione.
examples.en: Somebody grew rich on the funds intended for reconstruction.

examples.it: Temo che il nuovo capitolo impingui il volume senza arricchirlo.
examples.en: I fear the new chapter pads the volume without enriching it.

en: to advance with solemn, stately steps; to stride majestically
usage: Aulic verb for a slow, dignified, ceremonial walk ('incedere maestoso'), used also as a noun ('l'incedere della processione', 'l'incedere del tempo'). Defective: used practically only in the present, imperfect and gerund, with no participle in common use (passato remoto 'incedette' is very rare). Often ironic when applied to pompous people.

examples.it: La regina incedeva lentamente lungo la navata.
examples.en: The queen advanced slowly along the nave.

examples.it: Incede come se il corridoio dell'ufficio fosse una passerella.
examples.en: He struts along as if the office corridor were a catwalk.

examples.it: Incedendo con solennità, i cardinali entrarono nella cappella.
examples.en: Advancing solemnly, the cardinals entered the chapel.

en: to instil (fear, respect); to inspire (awe)
usage: Formal-literary, restricted to feelings of fear, awe or respect that a person or thing arouses in others ('incutere soggezione, terrore, rispetto'). Irregular like discutere: incussi, incusso. Everyday Italian prefers 'fare paura' or 'ispirare'.

examples.it: La sua sola presenza incuteva rispetto a tutti.
examples.en: His mere presence commanded everyone's respect.

examples.it: Il castello, di notte, incute un certo timore.
examples.en: At night the castle inspires a certain dread.

examples.it: Quelle minacce non gli incussero alcuna paura.
examples.en: Those threats did not frighten him at all.

en: to call, to announce officially (elections, a competition, a strike)
usage: Official-bureaucratic verb for formally proclaiming a public event: 'indire un referendum, uno sciopero, una gara d'appalto, un concorso'. Irregular like 'dire': indico, indici, indice; indissi; indetto; indirò. Never used for private invitations, where 'organizzare' or 'convocare' apply.

examples.it: Il presidente ha indetto le elezioni anticipate per il mese di marzo.
examples.en: The president has called early elections for March.

examples.it: I sindacati indissero uno sciopero generale di ventiquattro ore.
examples.en: The unions called a twenty-four-hour general strike.

examples.it: Se il comune indicesse un concorso, avresti buone possibilità.
examples.en: If the municipality announced a competitive exam, you would have a good chance.

en: to indulge in; to be lenient towards; to give way to
usage: Literary: to give in to a pleasure or weakness ('indulgere al sentimentalismo') or to be lenient towards someone ('indulgere verso i propri figli'); the noun is 'indulgenza' and 'indulto' is a pardon. Irregular: indulsi, indulto; takes avere. Note the preposition 'a', unlike English 'in'.

examples.it: Il film indulge troppo al patetico nella parte finale.
examples.en: The film indulges too much in pathos in its final part.

examples.it: Non ha mai indulto alle mode letterarie del momento.
examples.en: He never gave in to the literary fashions of the day.

examples.it: Un buon maestro indulge verso gli errori, non verso la pigrizia.
examples.en: A good teacher is lenient towards mistakes, not towards laziness.

en: to be inherent in, to pertain to, to concern
usage: Learned, juridical-philosophical verb governing 'a', found almost only in the third person and above all in the participle-adjective 'inerente' ('le spese inerenti al trasloco'); defective in practice, with the compound tenses hardly ever used. Conjugated with -isc- (inerisce). Note the common error 'inerente il': the correct construction is 'inerente a'.

examples.it: Il rischio inerisce alla natura stessa dell'attività d'impresa.
examples.en: Risk is inherent in the very nature of business activity.

examples.it: Sono deducibili solo i costi che ineriscono all'esercizio della professione.
examples.en: Only costs pertaining to the exercise of the profession are deductible.

examples.it: Il giudice ha escluso le questioni che non inerivano alla causa.
examples.en: The judge excluded the issues that did not pertain to the case.

en: to infer; to deduce; (inferire un colpo) to inflict, to strike
usage: Logical-scientific verb for drawing an inference ('se ne inferisce che...'), with the regular participle 'inferito'; in the literary sense of dealing a blow ('inferire una ferita, un colpo mortale') the participle is 'inferto' and the passato remoto 'infersi'. Conjugated with -isc- (inferisco).

examples.it: Dai dati raccolti si inferisce una chiara tendenza al calo.
examples.en: From the data collected a clear downward trend can be inferred.

examples.it: La notizia inferse un colpo durissimo alla sua reputazione.
examples.en: The news dealt a very hard blow to his reputation.

examples.it: Non è lecito inferire una regola generale da un solo caso.
examples.en: It is not legitimate to infer a general rule from a single case.

en: to be relentless towards; to rage against; to kick someone when they are down
usage: Formal-journalistic: to keep attacking a victim already defeated or helpless ('non infierire, ha già capito'), both physically ('infierire sul cadavere') and verbally; also of epidemics or storms raging over a region. Conjugated with -isc- (infierisco); regular.

examples.it: Non infierire su di lui: ha già ammesso l'errore.
examples.en: Don't rub it in: he has already admitted the mistake.

examples.it: Gli aggressori infierirono sulla vittima anche dopo che era caduta.
examples.en: The attackers kept hitting the victim even after she had fallen.

examples.it: La stampa infierirà sul ministro dopo questa gaffe.
examples.en: The press will be merciless towards the minister after this gaffe.

en: to meddle, to interfere (in others' affairs)
usage: Formal verb of political and juridical prose for unwarranted interference ('ingerirsi negli affari interni di uno stato'), the noun being 'ingerenza'. Conjugated with -isc- (mi ingerisco); do not confuse with the transitive 'ingerire' (to ingest, swallow). 'Intromettersi' and 'immischiarsi' are the everyday equivalents.

examples.it: Nessuno stato ha il diritto di ingerirsi negli affari interni di un altro.
examples.en: No state has the right to interfere in the internal affairs of another.

examples.it: Il vescovo si ingerì nella nomina del nuovo sindaco.
examples.en: The bishop meddled in the appointment of the new mayor.

examples.it: Non vorrei che il consiglio si ingerisse nelle scelte artistiche del direttore.
examples.en: I wouldn't want the board to interfere in the director's artistic choices.

en: to enjoin, to order formally; to serve notice on
usage: Juridical verb for a formal, binding order ('il giudice gli ingiunse di lasciare l'aula'); 'decreto ingiuntivo' is a court payment order. Irregular like 'giungere': ingiunsi, ingiunto. Note the construction with 'a qualcuno di fare', as with 'ordinare' and 'intimare'.

examples.it: Il tribunale ha ingiunto alla società di pagare entro quaranta giorni.
examples.en: The court ordered the company to pay within forty days.

examples.it: L'ufficiale ingiunse ai manifestanti di sciogliersi.
examples.en: The officer ordered the demonstrators to disperse.

examples.it: Se ti ingiungessero di sgomberare, cosa faresti?
examples.en: If they ordered you to vacate the premises, what would you do?

en: to be in league with; to have an understanding with; to have an affair with
usage: Pronominal idiom with fixed 'se la', slightly dated or ironic: to be secretly in agreement with someone, either for shady dealings ('se la intende con la concorrenza') or in a love affair. Irregular like intendere: me la intendo, se la intese, se la sono intesa; the participle stays feminine. Do not confuse with 'intendersene di' (to be an expert in).

examples.it: Pare che il custode se la intendesse con i ladri.
examples.en: It seems the caretaker was in league with the thieves.

examples.it: Tutti in ufficio sapevano che se la intendeva con la segretaria.
examples.en: Everyone in the office knew he was having an affair with the secretary.

examples.it: Se l'erano intesa fin dall'inizio per truccare la gara.
examples.en: They had been in cahoots from the start to rig the tender.

en: to ban; to bar (from office, from access); to declare legally incapable
usage: Juridical: to forbid access or activity ('interdire l'accesso ai non addetti'), to bar someone from public office as a penalty ('interdizione dai pubblici uffici'), or to declare a person legally incapable ('interdetto'). Irregular like dire: interdico, interdissi, interdetto; 'interdetto' also means dumbfounded.

examples.it: Il tribunale lo ha interdetto dai pubblici uffici per cinque anni.
examples.en: The court barred him from public office for five years.

examples.it: L'accesso alla zona è interdetto ai veicoli non autorizzati.
examples.en: Access to the area is prohibited for unauthorised vehicles.

examples.it: Chiesero che il vecchio fosse interdetto, giudicandolo incapace.
examples.en: They asked for the old man to be declared legally incapable.

en: to inveigh against, to rail at; to hurl abuse at
usage: Formal-journalistic verb for a violent verbal attack ('ha inveito contro l'arbitro'), always with 'contro'. Conjugated with -isc- (inveisco); the noun is 'invettiva'. 'Insultare' is the plain word, 'scagliarsi contro' the physical-verbal image, 'inveire' the sustained tirade.

examples.it: L'allenatore inveì contro l'arbitro e fu espulso.
examples.en: The coach railed at the referee and was sent off.

examples.it: Inveiva contro il governo con la solita retorica.
examples.en: He was inveighing against the government with the usual rhetoric.

examples.it: Non serve che tu inveisca contro di me: non decido io.
examples.en: There's no point hurling abuse at me: I'm not the one who decides.

en: to ensnare, to entrap; to beguile
usage: From 'rete' (net): to catch someone in a web of seduction, flattery or deceit ('irretito da false promesse'). Literary and journalistic; 'sedurre' can be neutral or positive, 'irretire' always implies entrapment, and 'adescare' is the legal term for luring. Conjugated with -isc- (irretisco).

examples.it: Il truffatore irretì decine di risparmiatori con la promessa di guadagni facili.
examples.en: The swindler ensnared dozens of savers with the promise of easy gains.

examples.it: Non lasciarti irretire dalle sue lusinghe.
examples.en: Don't let yourself be beguiled by his flattery.

examples.it: Temo che la setta lo abbia irretito completamente.
examples.en: I fear the sect has completely ensnared him.

en: to impose, to inflict (a penalty, a sanction)
usage: Strictly juridical: an authority 'irroga' a fine or penalty ('irrogare una sanzione disciplinare'); never used outside legal and administrative prose, where everyday Italian says 'infliggere' or 'dare una multa'. Regular -are verb with -ghi/-ghe spelling (irroghi); do not confuse with 'erogare' (to disburse) or 'irrorare' (to spray).

examples.it: L'Autorità ha irrogato alla società una sanzione di due milioni di euro.
examples.en: The Authority imposed a fine of two million euros on the company.

examples.it: La pena irrogata dal tribunale fu ridotta in appello.
examples.en: The sentence imposed by the court was reduced on appeal.

examples.it: Prima che venga irrogata la sanzione, l'interessato può presentare memorie difensive.
examples.en: Before the sanction is imposed, the party concerned may submit a written defence.

en: to languish; to pine away; to flag, to stagnate
usage: Literary verb for a slow decline of strength, love or activity: a prisoner 'langue in carcere', a conversation 'langue', an economy 'langue'. Conjugated with -isc- (languisco), but the poetic forms 'langue' and 'languono' survive in literature. Neutral alternatives: 'ristagnare' for activities, 'deperire' for health.

examples.it: Il prigioniero languì per anni in una cella umida.
examples.en: The prisoner languished for years in a damp cell.

examples.it: La conversazione languiva e nessuno sapeva come rianimarla.
examples.en: The conversation was flagging and nobody knew how to revive it.

examples.it: Senza investimenti, il settore continuerà a languire.
examples.en: Without investment, the sector will continue to stagnate.

en: to harm; to injure; to infringe (rights, interests)
usage: Juridical: an act 'lede' rights, interests, dignity or reputation ('ledere l'onore'); in medicine an organ may be 'leso'. The injured party is 'la parte lesa' and the injury 'la lesione'. Irregular: lesi, leso.

examples.it: La nuova norma lede il diritto alla riservatezza dei cittadini.
examples.en: The new rule infringes citizens' right to privacy.

examples.it: L'articolo ha leso gravemente la reputazione dell'azienda.
examples.en: The article seriously damaged the company's reputation.

examples.it: Nessun accordo potrà ledere gli interessi dei lavoratori.
examples.en: No agreement may harm the workers' interests.

en: to soothe, to alleviate (pain, grief)
usage: Learned verb, medical and literary, for easing physical or moral pain ('lenire le sofferenze'); the adjective 'lenitivo' names a soothing remedy. Conjugated with -isc- (lenisco). 'Alleviare' is the neutral term, 'calmare' the everyday one, 'lenire' the gentler and more elevated.

examples.it: Un impacco freddo lenisce il bruciore delle scottature.
examples.en: A cold compress soothes the burning of sunburn.

examples.it: Nulla poté lenire il dolore per la perdita del figlio.
examples.en: Nothing could ease the grief over the loss of her son.

examples.it: Speriamo che il tempo lenisca almeno in parte la sua amarezza.
examples.en: Let's hope time will soothe his bitterness at least in part.

en: to hover, to soar; to hang poised in the air
usage: Poetic verb (from 'libra', balance) for a bird, an aircraft or, figuratively, a thought held in perfect equilibrium above the ground ('librarsi in volo'). 'Volare' is neutral, 'planare' is technical gliding, 'librarsi' implies stillness and grace. Regular -are verb: 'mi libro, si libra' (stress on the i).

examples.it: L'aquila si librava immobile sopra la valle.
examples.en: The eagle hovered motionless above the valley.

examples.it: Il deltaplano si librò per qualche istante prima di scendere.
examples.en: The hang-glider hung poised for a few moments before descending.

examples.it: Vorrei che la mia mente potesse librarsi al di sopra delle preoccupazioni quotidiane.
examples.en: I wish my mind could soar above everyday worries.

en: to profit (from); to make money out of; to gain
usage: Formal and usually pejorative: to make money from something one should not exploit ('lucrare sulle disgrazie altrui'); juridical in 'a scopo di lucro'. Regular; the everyday verb is 'guadagnare' and the noun 'lucro'.

examples.it: Sono accusati di aver lucrato sulla vendita di mascherine.
examples.en: They are accused of having profiteered from the sale of masks.

examples.it: Non è un'associazione che lucra sulle rette degli studenti.
examples.en: It is not an organisation that makes money out of students' fees.

examples.it: Chi lucrerà davvero dalla privatizzazione?
examples.en: Who will really profit from the privatisation?

en: to forget (literary); to consign to oblivion
usage: Poetic and aulic equivalent of 'dimenticare', found in Foscolo and Leopardi and today only in deliberately elevated or ironic prose; the noun 'oblio' ('cadere nell'oblio') is far more current. Regular -are verb: 'oblio, oblii, oblia'.

examples.it: Il tempo oblia le ingiurie ma non le ingiustizie.
examples.en: Time forgets insults but not injustices.

examples.it: Chi obliò la propria patria non merita di ritrovarla.
examples.en: Whoever forgot his homeland does not deserve to find it again.

examples.it: Vorrei che quel giorno fosse obliato per sempre.
examples.en: I wish that day could be forgotten forever.

en: to occlude; to block (a vessel, a duct)
usage: Medical-technical for a vessel, duct or passage becoming blocked ('un trombo ha occluso l'arteria'), also in dentistry ('occlusione' is the bite) and meteorology ('fronte occluso'). Irregular like chiudere: occlusi, occluso. 'Ostruire' is the general synonym.

examples.it: Un coagulo ha occluso l'arteria coronaria.
examples.en: A clot occluded the coronary artery.

examples.it: Con il tempo il calcare occlude le tubature.
examples.en: Over time limescale blocks the pipes.

examples.it: Se il condotto si occludesse di nuovo, servirebbe un intervento.
examples.en: If the duct became blocked again, surgery would be needed.

en: to stand in the way; to be an obstacle (nulla osta)
usage: Bureaucratic-literary for being an obstacle, most familiar in 'nulla osta' (there is no objection), also the noun 'il nulla osta' (clearance, permit). The obstacle is usually the subject ('nulla ostava alla nomina'); personal forms such as 'io osto' also exist. The past participle, compound tenses and passato remoto are not used.

examples.it: Nulla osta al rilascio del permesso di soggiorno.
examples.en: There is no obstacle to issuing the residence permit.

examples.it: Nulla ostava a che il matrimonio fosse celebrato.
examples.en: Nothing stood in the way of the wedding being celebrated.

examples.it: Ho ottenuto il nulla osta della questura per lavorare all'estero.
examples.en: I got the police clearance to work abroad.

en: to comply with, to obey (an order, a ruling)
usage: Bureaucratic-juridical verb governing 'a': 'ottemperare agli obblighi di legge', 'giudizio di ottemperanza' (proceedings to enforce a ruling against the administration). Regular -are verb (ottèmpero). In everyday language one says 'rispettare' or 'obbedire a'; 'adempiere' is the near synonym for duties.

examples.it: L'azienda non ha ottemperato all'ordine di bonifica del sito.
examples.en: The company did not comply with the order to clean up the site.

examples.it: Il comune ottemperò alla sentenza solo dopo la nomina di un commissario.
examples.en: The municipality complied with the ruling only after a commissioner was appointed.

examples.it: Chi non ottemperi alle prescrizioni sarà sanzionato.
examples.en: Anyone who fails to comply with the requirements will be fined.

en: to dull; to blunt (the senses, the mind)
usage: Literary for blunting perception, intelligence or feeling ('la routine ottunde la sensibilità'); the participle survives above all as the adjective 'ottuso' (obtuse, dull-witted; angolo ottuso). Irregular: ottusi, ottuso; hardly ever used in the physical sense.

examples.it: L'alcol ottunde i riflessi e il giudizio.
examples.en: Alcohol dulls the reflexes and judgement.

examples.it: Anni di lavoro ripetitivo gli avevano ottuso la curiosità.
examples.en: Years of repetitive work had blunted his curiosity.

examples.it: È un farmaco che ottunderebbe la percezione del dolore.
examples.en: It is a drug that would dull the perception of pain.

en: to sponsor; to support officially; to represent (in court)
usage: Institutional: a public body 'patrocina' an event by lending its name ('con il patrocinio del Comune'); juridical for a lawyer representing a client ('patrocinio a spese dello Stato' is legal aid). Regular.

examples.it: La mostra è patrocinata dal Ministero della Cultura.
examples.en: The exhibition is sponsored by the Ministry of Culture.

examples.it: L'avvocato ha patrocinato la causa gratuitamente.
examples.en: The lawyer took on the case free of charge.

examples.it: Vorremmo che la Regione patrocinasse il festival.
examples.en: We would like the Region to give the festival its official backing.

en: to beat; to strike; to batter
usage: Juridical-literary for striking a person ('percosse e lesioni' is the offence of assault); in literary prose also of the sea beating the rocks or hands beating a drum. Irregular like scuotere: percossi, percosso; the plural noun 'le percosse' means a beating.

examples.it: È accusato di aver percosso la moglie ripetutamente.
examples.en: He is accused of having beaten his wife repeatedly.

examples.it: Le onde percuotevano gli scogli con violenza.
examples.en: The waves battered the rocks violently.

examples.it: I fedeli si percossero il petto in segno di penitenza.
examples.en: The faithful beat their breasts as a sign of penance.

en: to perish, to die (in an accident, a disaster)
usage: Literary and journalistic euphemism for a violent or collective death ('perirono in mare', 'gli operai periti nell'esplosione'); never used of a natural death at home. Conjugated with -isc- (perisco); auxiliary essere; the participle 'perito' is also a noun meaning expert surveyor, from a different root. Compare 'morire' (neutral) and 'soccombere' (to succumb).

examples.it: Centinaia di persone perirono nel naufragio.
examples.en: Hundreds of people perished in the shipwreck.

examples.it: È perito in un incidente stradale a soli trent'anni.
examples.en: He died in a road accident at only thirty.

examples.it: Chi di spada ferisce di spada perisce.
examples.en: He who lives by the sword dies by the sword.

en: to remain; to persist; to continue to be
usage: Formal-bureaucratic for a state or condition that persists ('permane lo stato di allerta', 'permangono dubbi'), commoner than 'rimanere' in reports and forecasts; the adjective 'permanente' derives from it. Irregular like rimanere: permango, permani; permasi; future permarrò; the participle is 'permaso' (rare) or 'permanuto'; takes essere.

examples.it: Permangono forti dubbi sulla sostenibilità del piano.
examples.en: Strong doubts remain about the sustainability of the plan.

examples.it: Il maltempo permarrà sulle regioni settentrionali fino a domenica.
examples.en: Bad weather will persist over the northern regions until Sunday.

examples.it: È necessario che il paziente permanga in osservazione per una notte.
examples.en: The patient needs to remain under observation for one night.

en: to permeate; to pervade, to imbue
usage: Scientific (of liquids passing through membranes) and figurative-intellectual: an idea or a mood 'permea' a text, an epoch, a society ('una cultura permeata di scetticismo'). Often passive with 'di'. Regular -are verb: 'pèrmeo' (stress on the first e). 'Pervadere' is the close synonym; 'impregnare' more physical.

examples.it: Un senso di precarietà permea tutto il romanzo.
examples.en: A sense of precariousness permeates the whole novel.

examples.it: L'acqua permeò lentamente lo strato di argilla.
examples.en: The water slowly permeated the layer of clay.

examples.it: La sua opera è permeata di una religiosità inquieta.
examples.en: His work is imbued with a restless religiosity.

en: to plead (a cause); to argue eloquently for
usage: Literary-rhetorical, almost always in 'perorare la causa di' (to plead someone's cause); the noun 'perorazione' is the closing appeal of a speech. Regular.

examples.it: Il senatore perorò con passione la causa dei minatori.
examples.en: The senator passionately pleaded the miners' cause.

examples.it: Ha perorato per anni la creazione di un parco nazionale.
examples.en: For years he argued for the creation of a national park.

examples.it: Nessuno perorerà la nostra causa se non lo facciamo noi.
examples.en: No one will plead our cause if we don't do it ourselves.

en: to pervade; to permeate; to spread through
usage: Literary-journalistic for a feeling, atmosphere or smell filling a place or person completely ('un senso di pace pervadeva la stanza', 'pervaso dal dubbio'); 'pervasivo' is the adjective. Irregular like invadere: pervasi, pervaso.

examples.it: Un profumo di pane appena sfornato pervadeva tutta la casa.
examples.en: A smell of freshly baked bread pervaded the whole house.

examples.it: Dopo la notizia fu pervaso da un'inquietudine sorda.
examples.en: After the news he was filled with a dull unease.

examples.it: Temo che questo cinismo pervada anche i più giovani.
examples.en: I fear this cynicism is spreading to the very young as well.

en: to seize, to attach (goods, wages) for debt; to distrain
usage: Juridical-financial for the court-ordered seizure of a debtor's assets or wages ('pignorare un quinto dello stipendio'); the noun is 'pignoramento'. Regular. 'Sequestrare' is the criminal-law seizure, 'confiscare' the definitive one.

examples.it: Gli hanno pignorato l'auto per un debito con il fisco.
examples.en: His car was seized over a debt to the tax authorities.

examples.it: La banca pignorerà la casa se le rate non vengono pagate.
examples.en: The bank will seize the house if the instalments are not paid.

examples.it: Temono che il tribunale pignori anche i conti correnti.
examples.en: They fear the court will attach their bank accounts too.

en: to postulate; to assume as a premise; to require
usage: Scientific-philosophical for assuming something as a starting point without proof ('la teoria postula l'esistenza di particelle invisibili'); a 'postulato' is an axiom. Regular; 'presupporre' is the general synonym.

examples.it: Euclide postulò che per due punti passi una sola retta.
examples.en: Euclid postulated that only one straight line passes through two points.

examples.it: Il modello postula una crescita costante della domanda.
examples.en: The model assumes constant growth in demand.

examples.it: Non possiamo postulare ciò che dovremmo dimostrare.
examples.en: We cannot postulate what we ought to prove.

en: to be a prelude to; to foreshadow; to lead up to
usage: Formal-journalistic, always with 'a': an event or sign 'prelude' to what follows ('nubi che preludono al temporale', 'una mossa che prelude alle dimissioni'). Irregular like alludere: prelusi, preluso; takes avere. Musical 'preludio' is the noun.

examples.it: Il calo delle vendite preludeva alla chiusura dello stabilimento.
examples.en: The fall in sales was a prelude to the plant's closure.

examples.it: Questo incontro prelude a una collaborazione più ampia.
examples.en: This meeting paves the way for a broader collaboration.

examples.it: Quei silenzi prelusero alla rottura definitiva.
examples.en: Those silences led up to the final break.

en: to abuse one's power; to overstep; to ride roughshod over
usage: Formal-political: to impose oneself on others through abuse of authority or force ('prevaricare sui più deboli'); the noun 'prevaricazione' names bullying and abuse of office. Regular; spelling prevarichi, prevarichiamo. Note it is not the English 'prevaricate' (to evade), which is 'tergiversare'.

examples.it: Il dirigente prevaricava continuamente sui suoi collaboratori.
examples.en: The manager constantly rode roughshod over his staff.

examples.it: Chi ha prevaricato per anni ora dovrà rispondere delle proprie azioni.
examples.en: Those who abused their power for years will now have to answer for their actions.

examples.it: È inaccettabile che la maggioranza prevarichi sulle minoranze.
examples.en: It is unacceptable for the majority to trample on minorities.

en: to procure, to obtain (with effort); (procacciarsi) to get oneself (a living, clients)
usage: Literary-commercial verb for obtaining something through activity and effort, often reflexive: 'procacciarsi il cibo', 'procacciarsi clienti'; the 'procacciatore d'affari' is a business intermediary. Regular -are verb (procaccio, procacci). 'Procurare' is the neutral synonym; 'procacciare' adds the idea of hunting.

examples.it: Si procacciava da vivere con piccoli lavori occasionali.
examples.en: He earned his living with small odd jobs.

examples.it: L'agente procacciò all'azienda contratti in tutta Europa.
examples.en: The agent procured contracts for the company all over Europe.

examples.it: Chi ha bisogno di procacciarsi il cibo ogni giorno non ha tempo per la filosofia.
examples.en: Those who must hunt for food every day have no time for philosophy.

en: to lavish; to pour out (energy, praise, money); (profondersi) to be profuse in
usage: Literary-formal for spending something abundantly ('profondere energie, denaro, lodi'); the pronominal 'profondersi in scuse / ringraziamenti / complimenti' is the usual form, often ironic about excess. Irregular like fondere: profusi, profuso; 'profusione' is the noun.

examples.it: Ha profuso tutte le sue energie nel progetto.
examples.en: He poured all his energy into the project.

examples.it: Il direttore si profuse in scuse per il disguido.
examples.en: The manager was profuse in his apologies for the mix-up.

examples.it: Non è necessario che vi profondiate in ringraziamenti.
examples.en: There is no need for you to be so effusive in your thanks.

en: to divulge, to spread (secrets, rumours)
usage: Learned, juridical-journalistic verb for spreading information that should have stayed confidential ('propalare segreti d'ufficio'), with a nuance of indiscretion or malice. 'Divulgare' is neutral, 'spifferare' colloquial, 'propalare' formal and disapproving. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Qualcuno ha propalato il contenuto degli interrogatori alla stampa.
examples.en: Somebody leaked the content of the interrogations to the press.

examples.it: Propalava voci infondate sui colleghi per screditarli.
examples.en: He spread groundless rumours about his colleagues to discredit them.

examples.it: Il funzionario fu sospeso per aver propalato informazioni riservate.
examples.en: The official was suspended for having divulged confidential information.

en: to burst out; to break into (tears, laughter, applause)
usage: Literary-journalistic verb for a sudden, irrepressible outburst ('il pubblico proruppe in un applauso'); a close synonym of 'erompere', and the standard formal alternative to 'scoppiare a piangere/ridere'. Irregular like 'rompere': proruppi, prorotto (participle rare); auxiliary essere. The adjective 'prorompente' (exuberant) is common.

examples.it: Alla notizia la madre proruppe in singhiozzi.
examples.en: At the news the mother burst into sobs.

examples.it: Il pubblico è prorotto in una risata liberatoria.
examples.en: The audience burst into liberating laughter.

examples.it: Temo che, se glielo dici, prorompa in una delle sue sfuriate.
examples.en: I fear that if you tell him, he will burst into one of his rages.

en: to acquit; to clear (of a charge); to release (from an obligation)
usage: Juridical: to declare someone not guilty or drop the charge before trial ('prosciolto per non aver commesso il fatto'); also formal for releasing someone from a vow or promise. Irregular like sciogliere: prosciolgo, prosciolsi, prosciolto. 'Assolvere' is the acquittal at trial, 'scagionare' the clearing of suspicion.

examples.it: Il giudice ha prosciolto tutti gli imputati per insufficienza di prove.
examples.en: The judge acquitted all the defendants for insufficient evidence.

examples.it: Fu prosciolta dall'accusa di riciclaggio dopo due anni.
examples.en: She was cleared of the money-laundering charge after two years.

examples.it: Il papa lo prosciolse dal voto di castità.
examples.en: The pope released him from his vow of chastity.

en: to itch
usage: Used in the third person with the body part as subject and the person as indirect object ('mi prude il naso', 'gli prudono le mani' = he is itching to hit someone). Defective: it has no past participle and no compound tenses; for those use 'avere prurito'.

examples.it: Mi prude la schiena e non riesco a grattarmi.
examples.en: My back itches and I can't scratch it.

examples.it: Dopo la puntura gli prudeva tutto il braccio.
examples.en: After the sting his whole arm was itching.

examples.it: Se ti prudessero le mani, conterei fino a dieci prima di reagire.
examples.en: If you were itching to hit someone, I'd count to ten before reacting.

en: to swarm, to teem; to spring up everywhere, to proliferate
usage: From the Latin 'pullulare' (to sprout): of living things multiplying and of places teeming with them ('la città pullula di turisti'); also of things springing up everywhere ('pullulano i negozi di telefonia'). Journalistic and literary; 'brulicare' stresses movement, 'pullulare' abundance and proliferation. Regular -are verb (pùllulo).

examples.it: Il quartiere pullula di locali alla moda.
examples.en: The neighbourhood is teeming with trendy bars.

examples.it: Nel dopoguerra pullularono i piccoli partiti.
examples.en: In the post-war period small parties sprang up everywhere.

examples.it: Temo che la rete pullulerà sempre di notizie false.
examples.en: I fear the internet will always be swarming with fake news.

en: to inform in detail, to brief; to compare, to equate
usage: Formal-administrative verb for giving a full account ('la ragguaglierò sugli sviluppi'), the noun being 'ragguaglio' (detailed report); the older sense of making equal or comparing survives in accounting ('interesse ragguagliato ad anno'). Regular -are verb. 'Informare' and 'aggiornare' are the everyday alternatives.

examples.it: Il ministro fu ragguagliato sulla situazione al confine.
examples.en: The minister was briefed on the situation at the border.

examples.it: Vi ragguaglierò non appena avrò notizie certe.
examples.en: I will bring you up to date as soon as I have reliable news.

examples.it: Il tasso è ragguagliato ad anno secondo la prassi bancaria.
examples.en: The rate is expressed on an annual basis according to banking practice.

en: to congeal; to clot; to set, to thicken
usage: Technical-culinary and medical for a liquid thickening into a solid mass: blood 'si rapprende' (clots), a sauce, custard or cement 'si rapprende' (sets). Irregular like prendere: si rapprende, si rapprese, rappreso; the transitive 'rapprendere' is rare.

examples.it: Il sangue si è rappreso intorno alla ferita.
examples.en: The blood has clotted around the wound.

examples.it: Mescola finché la crema non si rapprende.
examples.en: Stir until the custard thickens.

examples.it: Se il latte si rapprendesse, la ricetta sarebbe da rifare.
examples.en: If the milk curdled, the recipe would have to be done again.

en: to recognise, to identify; to see, to discern (in something)
patterns: ravvisare gli estremi di un reato
usage: Formal, juridical-journalistic verb: to identify a quality or a fact in something ('ravvisare gli estremi del reato', to find the elements of a crime; 'non ravviso alcun motivo per'). Also to recognise a person ('lo ravvisò dal passo'). Regular -are verb. 'Riconoscere' is neutral, 'scorgere' perceptual.

examples.it: Il pubblico ministero non ha ravvisato gli estremi del reato.
examples.en: The public prosecutor did not find the elements of a crime.

examples.it: In quella scelta molti ravvisarono un segnale di debolezza.
examples.en: Many saw in that choice a sign of weakness.

examples.it: Non ravviso alcuna contraddizione tra le due dichiarazioni.
examples.en: I see no contradiction between the two statements.

en: to balk, to resist stubbornly; (of animals) to kick back
usage: Literally of a mule or horse kicking against the spur; figuratively, and often with humour, of a person who resists every attempt to persuade them ('recalcitra all'idea di trasferirsi'). The adjective 'recalcitrante' is far more common than the verb. Regular -are verb (recàlcitro).

examples.it: Il mulo recalcitrava e non voleva attraversare il ponte.
examples.en: The mule was balking and refused to cross the bridge.

examples.it: Recalcitrò a lungo prima di accettare la nomina.
examples.en: He resisted for a long time before accepting the appointment.

examples.it: Per quanto recalcitri, dovrà firmare anche lui.
examples.en: However much he balks, he will have to sign too.

en: to cut off, to sever (cleanly); to break off (ties)
usage: Literary and technical verb for a clean cut with a blade: flowers, branches, a rope and, figuratively, ties and relationships ('recidere ogni legame con il passato'). 'Tagliare' is neutral, 'troncare' more abrupt, 'mozzare' for limbs. Irregular like 'decidere': recisi, reciso; the adjective 'reciso' also means curt, flat (un rifiuto reciso).

examples.it: Il giardiniere recise le rose appassite con un colpo secco.
examples.en: The gardener cut off the withered roses with a sharp snip.

examples.it: Con quella lettera recise ogni rapporto con la famiglia.
examples.en: With that letter he severed all ties with his family.

examples.it: Bisogna che il chirurgo recida il tendine danneggiato.
examples.en: The surgeon needs to sever the damaged tendon.

en: to rebuke, to reprimand sharply
usage: Formal verb for a stern reproof from a superior ('il giudice redarguì l'avvocato'). Conjugated with -isc- (redarguisco). 'Rimproverare' is the everyday term, 'ammonire' a warning, 'rimbrottare' a grumbling scolding; 'redarguire' is the sharpest and most official.

examples.it: Il presidente redarguì aspramente il deputato per le sue parole.
examples.en: The speaker sharply rebuked the deputy for his words.

examples.it: Fu redarguito davanti a tutti i colleghi.
examples.en: He was reprimanded in front of all his colleagues.

examples.it: Non voglio che tu lo redarguisca in pubblico: parlagli in privato.
examples.en: I don't want you to reprimand him in public: talk to him privately.

en: to redeem; to deliver (from sin, slavery, debt)
usage: Religious, moral and historical verb: Christ 'redime' humanity, a hero 'redime' the oppressed, a sinner 'si redime' (auxiliary essere); in old legal usage also to buy back a mortgaged property. Irregular: redensi, redento. 'Riscattare' is the secular synonym.

examples.it: Sperava di redimersi dagli errori del passato.
examples.en: He hoped to redeem himself from the mistakes of the past.

examples.it: Secondo la dottrina, Cristo redense l'umanità con il suo sacrificio.
examples.en: According to doctrine, Christ redeemed humanity with his sacrifice.

examples.it: Nessuna donazione potrà redimere un'intera vita di soprusi.
examples.en: No donation will be able to redeem an entire life of abuses.

en: to shine brightly, to glow; to stand out (of virtues)
usage: Aulic verb (Dante, Petrarch) for a brilliant light, extended to glory and virtue ('rifulse per il suo coraggio'), sometimes ironic today ('non ha certo rifulso per originalità'). Irregular and defective: passato remoto 'rifulsi', participle 'rifulso' rare; auxiliary essere or avere. 'Risplendere' is the neutral synonym.

examples.it: La luna rifulgeva sul mare calmo.
examples.en: The moon shone brightly on the calm sea.

examples.it: In quella battaglia rifulse il valore dei difensori.
examples.en: In that battle the valour of the defenders shone forth.

examples.it: Il suo discorso non ha certo rifulso per chiarezza.
examples.en: His speech certainly did not stand out for clarity.

en: to scold, to grumble at; to reproach
usage: Familiar and picturesque verb for a grumbling, ill-tempered scolding, typical of parents and grandparents ('la nonna lo rimbrottava per il disordine'); the noun is 'rimbrotto'. Milder and more domestic than 'redarguire' or 'rampognare'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Lo rimbrottò per essere tornato tardi senza avvisare.
examples.en: She scolded him for coming home late without letting her know.

examples.it: Mi rimbrottava continuamente, ma con affetto.
examples.en: He was forever grumbling at me, but affectionately.

examples.it: Se lo rimbrotti ancora, finirà per non ascoltarti più.
examples.en: If you keep scolding him, he'll end up not listening to you any more.

en: to be sorry (mi rincresce = I regret); to regret
usage: Formal-polite impersonal construction like 'dispiacere': 'mi rincresce' (I am sorry), 'mi rincresce doverle dire' in letters, 'se non le rincresce' (if you don't mind). Irregular like crescere: rincresce, rincrebbe, rincresciuto; takes essere and is used only in the third person.

examples.it: Mi rincresce di non poter accettare il suo invito.
examples.en: I regret that I cannot accept your invitation.

examples.it: Le rincrebbe molto che nessuno l'avesse avvertita.
examples.en: She was very sorry that no one had warned her.

examples.it: Se non vi rincresce, vorrei chiudere la finestra.
examples.en: If you don't mind, I'd like to close the window.

en: to find, to discover (by chance or in a search); to come round, to regain consciousness
usage: Two senses that fix the auxiliary: transitive 'rinvenire' (aux avere) is the police-and-archaeology verb for finding a body, an object or traces ('sono stati rinvenuti reperti romani'); intransitive 'rinvenire' (aux essere) means to regain consciousness ('è rinvenuta dopo pochi minuti'). Irregular like venire: rinvengo, rinvenni, rinvenuto.

examples.it: I sommozzatori hanno rinvenuto il relitto a quaranta metri di profondità.
examples.en: The divers found the wreck at a depth of forty metres.

examples.it: La ferita rinvenne solo in ambulanza.
examples.en: The injured woman came round only in the ambulance.

examples.it: Se rinvenissero l'arma, il caso sarebbe risolto.
examples.en: If they found the weapon, the case would be solved.

en: to recover one's losses from; to seek redress from; to get one's own back
usage: Juridical-financial: an insurer or creditor 'si rivale' on the person responsible to recover what it paid (whence 'rivalsa'); figuratively, to take revenge for a wrong. Irregular like valere: mi rivalgo, mi rivalsi, rivalso; future mi rivarrò.

examples.it: L'assicurazione si rivarrà sul conducente ubriaco per i danni pagati.
examples.en: The insurer will recover from the drunk driver the damages it paid.

examples.it: Il datore di lavoro si è rivalso sul dipendente per l'ammanco.
examples.en: The employer sought redress from the employee for the shortfall.

examples.it: Non rivalerti sui figli per i torti subiti dal loro padre.
examples.en: Don't take out on the children the wrongs their father did you.

en: to jeer at, to ridicule; to make fun of openly
usage: Intensive of 'beffare': to mock someone loudly and publicly, with a hint of cruelty ('sbeffeggiato dai compagni'); frequent in sports and political journalism. 'Deridere' is more neutral, 'schernire' more contemptuous, 'sfottere' colloquial. Regular -are verb (sbeffeggio, sbeffeggi).

examples.it: I tifosi avversari sbeffeggiarono il portiere per tutta la partita.
examples.en: The opposing fans jeered at the goalkeeper for the whole match.

examples.it: Il comico ha sbeffeggiato i politici di ogni schieramento.
examples.en: The comedian ridiculed politicians of every stripe.

examples.it: Non sopporto che si sbeffeggi chi ha il coraggio di tentare.
examples.en: I can't stand people jeering at those who have the courage to try.

en: to dismay, to stun; (sbigottirsi) to be dumbfounded
usage: To leave someone speechless with shock or dismay; the participle 'sbigottito' ('rimase sbigottito') is the most used form. Conjugated with -isc- (sbigottisco); transitive with avere, intransitive and pronominal with essere. 'Sconvolgere' is stronger, 'stupire' weaker, 'sbigottire' adds bewilderment and fear.

examples.it: La notizia sbigottì l'intero paese.
examples.en: The news stunned the whole village.

examples.it: Restammo sbigottiti davanti a tanta crudeltà.
examples.en: We were dumbfounded by such cruelty.

examples.it: È sbigottita nel vedere quanto era cambiato.
examples.en: She was stunned to see how much he had changed.

en: to sound (the depths); to probe, to explore thoroughly
usage: Nautical term (to measure depth with a 'scandaglio', sounding line) used figuratively for probing minds, texts or situations in depth ('scandagliare le intenzioni dell'avversario'). Journalistic and literary; 'sondare' is the near synonym, 'esplorare' more general. Regular -are verb (scandaglio, scandagli).

examples.it: I sommozzatori scandagliarono il fondale per ore.
examples.en: The divers sounded the seabed for hours.

examples.it: Il romanzo scandaglia con lucidità le contraddizioni della borghesia.
examples.en: The novel probes the contradictions of the bourgeoisie with lucidity.

examples.it: Prima di decidere, vorrei che scandagliassimo ogni alternativa.
examples.en: Before deciding, I would like us to explore every alternative thoroughly.

en: to mock, to scorn; to deride contemptuously
usage: Literary verb for contemptuous mockery ('scherniva la sua fede'); the noun 'scherno' ('fatto oggetto di scherno') is common in formal prose. Conjugated with -isc- (schernisco). 'Deridere' is neutral, 'sbeffeggiare' loud and public, 'schernire' cold and disdainful.

examples.it: I soldati schernivano il prigioniero.
examples.en: The soldiers were mocking the prisoner.

examples.it: Fu schernito dai colleghi per le sue idee.
examples.en: He was scorned by his colleagues for his ideas.

examples.it: Chi schernisce i deboli rivela solo la propria miseria.
examples.en: Whoever mocks the weak reveals only his own wretchedness.

en: to hang out (washing); to reel off, to parade (knowledge, figures)
usage: Literally to hang out laundry to dry in the sun (Tuscan); figuratively and ironically, to display a long series of names, figures or citations to impress ('sciorinare statistiche'). Regular -are verb. 'Snocciolare' is the close colloquial synonym; 'ostentare' more general.

examples.it: Il ministro sciorinò una serie di cifre a memoria.
examples.en: The minister reeled off a series of figures from memory.

examples.it: La nonna sciorinava le lenzuola sul terrazzo.
examples.en: Grandmother would hang the sheets out on the terrace.

examples.it: Ha sciorinato citazioni in latino per mezz'ora.
examples.en: He paraded Latin quotations for half an hour.

en: to whip, to lash; to lash out at (with words); (of wind) to buffet
usage: From 'sferza' (whip): literally to lash, figuratively of biting satire or reproach ('sferzare i costumi del tempo') and of wind, rain or hail beating on something. Journalistic-literary; 'frustare' is the physical verb, 'fustigare' the moral one, 'sferzare' both. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Un vento gelido sferzava le facce dei pescatori.
examples.en: An icy wind lashed the fishermen's faces.

examples.it: Il commediografo sferzò i vizi della nobiltà con feroce ironia.
examples.en: The playwright lashed the vices of the nobility with ferocious irony.

examples.it: Temo che la stampa lo sferzi ancora più duramente dopo questa gaffe.
examples.en: I fear the press will lash him even harder after this blunder.

en: to incite secretly, to stir up; to instigate (to revolt)
usage: Spregiativo verb for whipping people up to disorder by underhand means; a 'sobillatore' is an agitator. Compared with 'istigare' (neutral-juridical) and 'aizzare' (open, violent), 'sobillare' implies secret and persistent manoeuvring behind the scenes. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Furono accusati di aver sobillato la folla contro il governatore.
examples.en: They were accused of having stirred up the crowd against the governor.

examples.it: Qualcuno sobilla gli operai per far saltare la trattativa.
examples.en: Somebody is stirring up the workers to wreck the negotiation.

examples.it: Non credo che li abbia sobillati lui: la rabbia era già diffusa.
examples.en: I don't think he incited them: the anger was already widespread.

en: to succumb; to be defeated; to give way
usage: Formal for yielding to a stronger force, illness or temptation ('soccombere alla malattia') and juridical for losing a case ('la parte soccombente' pays the costs). Takes essere; the participle 'soccombuto' is rare, so compound tenses are seldom used.

examples.it: L'esercito soccombette dopo un assedio di tre mesi.
examples.en: The army succumbed after a three-month siege.

examples.it: Le spese legali sono a carico della parte che soccombe.
examples.en: Legal costs are borne by the losing party.

examples.it: Temo che l'azienda soccomba alla concorrenza straniera.
examples.en: I fear the company will succumb to foreign competition.

en: to be subject to; to be liable to; to submit to
usage: Juridical-formal, always with 'a': to be subject to a law, tax, sanction or authority ('i redditi soggiacciono a tassazione'); literary for yielding to a force or passion. Irregular like giacere: soggiaccio, soggiacqui, soggiaciuto; takes essere.

examples.it: Questi contratti soggiacciono alla legge del paese in cui sono firmati.
examples.en: These contracts are subject to the law of the country where they are signed.

examples.it: Anche i sovrani soggiacevano al giudizio della Chiesa.
examples.en: Even sovereigns were subject to the judgement of the Church.

examples.it: Chi non rispetta il divieto soggiacerà a una sanzione pecuniaria.
examples.en: Anyone who disregards the ban will be liable to a fine.

en: to subjugate, to subdue; to dominate (a person, an audience)
usage: From 'giogo' (yoke): historical-political for conquering and subjecting peoples, and psychological for the dominating power of a personality or a gaze ('soggiogato dal suo fascino'). 'Sottomettere' is neutral, 'assoggettare' formal, 'soggiogare' the most vivid. Regular -are verb with -ghi/-ghe spelling.

examples.it: Roma soggiogò le tribù galliche in meno di dieci anni.
examples.en: Rome subjugated the Gallic tribes in less than ten years.

examples.it: Era soggiogato dalla personalità del maestro.
examples.en: He was under the spell of the master's personality.

examples.it: Nessun oratore soggiogherà mai una platea così scettica.
examples.en: No orator will ever dominate such a sceptical audience.

en: to be in the habit of; to be wont to; to usually do
usage: Literary verb of habit, alive today mainly in the fixed 'come si suol dire' (as they say) and in 'essere solito fare'. Irregular and defective: present soglio, suoli, suole, sogliamo, solete, sogliono; subjunctive soglia; imperfect solevo; the participle 'solito' is now only an adjective; no passato remoto, future, conditional or imperative.

examples.it: Come si suol dire, chi dorme non piglia pesci.
examples.en: As they say, the early bird catches the worm.

examples.it: Da giovane soleva passeggiare ogni sera lungo il fiume.
examples.en: When young he used to walk along the river every evening.

examples.it: I poeti sogliono cantare ciò che hanno perduto.
examples.en: Poets are wont to sing of what they have lost.

en: to lull; to quieten; to calm down (a dispute, a passion)
usage: Literary-journalistic for temporarily quieting a conflict, anger or passion without resolving it ('sopire le polemiche'); the participle 'sopito' is common as an adjective for dormant feelings ('rancori mai sopiti'). Conjugated with -isc- (sopisco); regular.

examples.it: Il compromesso ha sopito le polemiche, ma non le ha risolte.
examples.en: The compromise has quietened the controversy, but not resolved it.

examples.it: L'incontro riaccese passioni che credeva sopite da anni.
examples.en: The meeting rekindled passions she thought had lain dormant for years.

examples.it: Sarà difficile che una dichiarazione sopisca la rabbia dei lavoratori.
examples.en: A statement is unlikely to calm the workers' anger.

en: to overwhelm; to overpower; to overcome
usage: Physical overpowering ('sopraffatti dal numero dei nemici') and, most often, emotional: 'sopraffatto dall'emozione, dalla stanchezza, dagli eventi'. Irregular like fare: sopraffaccio (or sopraffò), sopraffai, sopraffà; sopraffeci; sopraffatto; future sopraffarò. The noun is 'sopraffazione' (abuse of power).

examples.it: Sopraffatto dall'emozione, non riuscì a finire il discorso.
examples.en: Overcome with emotion, he could not finish his speech.

examples.it: I difensori furono sopraffatti dal numero degli assalitori.
examples.en: The defenders were overpowered by the sheer number of attackers.

examples.it: Non lasciare che la paura ti sopraffaccia.
examples.en: Don't let fear overwhelm you.

en: to have (an effect); to produce (a result); to obtain by lot
