usage: Formal, almost only in 'sortire effetto' and 'sortire un esito' ('le minacce non sortirono alcun effetto'), conjugated with -isc- (sortisce). A homonymous regional-military 'sortire' (sorto, aux essere) means to go out or make a sortie; do not confuse with 'uscire'. Regular.

examples.it: Le proteste non hanno sortito alcun effetto sul governo.
examples.en: The protests had no effect whatsoever on the government.

examples.it: La cura sortì un esito migliore del previsto.
examples.en: The treatment produced a better outcome than expected.

examples.it: Dubito che un ultimatum sortisca l'effetto sperato.
examples.en: I doubt an ultimatum will have the hoped-for effect.

en: to leave unsaid; to keep quiet about; to pass over in silence
usage: Formal-journalistic for deliberately omitting a fact from an account ('il rapporto sottace i costi reali'); more pointed than 'tacere' because it implies concealment. Irregular like tacere: sottaccio, sottacqui, sottaciuto.

examples.it: Il comunicato sottace le vere ragioni delle dimissioni.
examples.en: The statement leaves the real reasons for the resignation unsaid.

examples.it: Non va sottaciuto che il progetto ha già superato il budget.
examples.en: It should not be passed over that the project has already exceeded its budget.

examples.it: L'autore sottacque per anni la propria appartenenza al partito.
examples.en: For years the author kept quiet about his party membership.

en: to overwhelm, to overpower; to exceed; to oppress
usage: Literary verb for a force that exceeds and crushes another: an army, a wave, a feeling ('soverchiato dal dolore'), or an overbearing person who bullies ('soverchieria' is bullying). 'Sopraffare' is the neutral synonym, 'sovrastare' just to tower over. Regular -are verb (soverchio, soverchi).

examples.it: Le forze nemiche soverchiavano di gran lunga le nostre.
examples.en: The enemy forces far outnumbered ours.

examples.it: Fu soverchiato da un'emozione che non riuscì a controllare.
examples.en: He was overwhelmed by an emotion he could not control.

examples.it: Non permettere che i più forti soverchino i più deboli.
examples.en: Don't allow the stronger to bully the weaker.

en: to come to mind; (literary) to aid, to relieve
usage: Literary: 'mi sovviene' means 'it comes back to me' or 'I recall', famous from Leopardi ('e mi sovvien l'eterno'); with a direct object it is the archaic 'to help', whence 'sovvenzione'. Irregular like venire: sovviene, sovvenne, sovvenuto; takes essere and is used almost only in the third person.

examples.it: Non mi sovviene il nome di quel pittore.
examples.en: That painter's name escapes me.

examples.it: Le sovvenne all'improvviso che aveva lasciato il gas acceso.
examples.en: It suddenly came back to her that she had left the gas on.

examples.it: Se ti sovvenisse qualche dettaglio, chiamami pure.
examples.en: If any detail should come back to you, do call me.

en: to pine; to be consumed (with longing, grief); to melt
usage: Literary for being consumed by an intense feeling ('struggersi di nostalgia, d'amore, di gelosia'); the adjective 'struggente' (heart-rending) and noun 'struggimento' are common in reviews. Irregular like distruggere: mi struggo, mi strussi, strutto; the transitive 'struggere' (to melt) is archaic.

examples.it: Si struggeva di nostalgia per la sua terra.
examples.en: He was consumed with longing for his homeland.

examples.it: Mi struggo dal desiderio di rivederla.
examples.en: I am aching with the desire to see her again.

examples.it: Si strusse per mesi senza avere notizie del figlio.
examples.en: She pined for months without news of her son.

en: to substitute; to replace (formally); to stand in for
usage: Juridical-institutional for replacing a person in an office or a thing with an equivalent ('surrogare il consigliere dimissionario'); the noun 'surrogato' is a poor substitute (surrogato del caffè) and 'maternità surrogata' is surrogacy. Regular; spelling surroghi.

examples.it: Il consiglio ha surrogato il membro decaduto con il primo dei non eletti.
examples.en: The council replaced the disqualified member with the first runner-up.

examples.it: Nessuna tecnologia potrà surrogare il contatto umano.
examples.en: No technology will be able to substitute for human contact.

examples.it: Durante la guerra si surrogava il caffè con l'orzo tostato.
examples.en: During the war coffee was replaced with roasted barley.

en: to slip away; to sneak off; to make oneself scarce
usage: Colloquial pronominal idiom with fixed 'se la': to leave quietly to avoid trouble or work ('se l'è svignata prima del conto'); synonyms are 'squagliarsela' and 'filarsela'. Regular; takes essere with the invariable feminine participle ('se la sono svignata').

examples.it: Appena è arrivato il capo, se l'è svignata dalla porta sul retro.
examples.en: As soon as the boss arrived, he slipped out the back door.

examples.it: I ragazzi se la svignarono senza pagare.
examples.en: The lads sneaked off without paying.

examples.it: Non svignartela proprio adesso che c'è da pulire!
examples.en: Don't make yourself scarce right now that there's cleaning to do!

en: to compromise, to come to terms; to make concessions
usage: Juridical verb (to settle a dispute by mutual concession, 'transazione') that in ordinary formal usage appears mostly in the negative: 'su questo non transigo' (I won't compromise on this). Irregular: passato remoto 'transigei' or 'transigetti', participle 'transatto', practically used only in legal texts.

examples.it: Sulla sicurezza dei lavoratori non transigo.
examples.en: On workers' safety I make no compromises.

examples.it: Le parti transigettero la lite prima dell'udienza.
examples.en: The parties settled the dispute before the hearing.

examples.it: È un uomo che non transigerebbe mai sui principi.
examples.en: He is a man who would never compromise on principles.

en: to be astounded, to be amazed beyond words
usage: Expressive verb (literally 'to go out of the century', out of the world) for total astonishment, often with a comic tone ('trasecolò nel vedere il conto'). Regular -are verb; auxiliary essere or avere. Stronger than 'stupirsi'; 'strabiliare' and 'sbalordire' are the near synonyms, 'trasecolare' the most bookish.

examples.it: Trasecolai quando seppi che aveva lasciato tutto per fare il pescatore.
examples.en: I was astounded when I learned he had left everything to become a fisherman.

examples.it: I genitori sono trasecolati davanti alla pagella.
examples.en: The parents were dumbfounded at the report card.

examples.it: C'è da trasecolare a sentire certe dichiarazioni.
examples.en: It's enough to make you gasp, hearing certain statements.

en: to show through; to shine through; to be visible (of feelings)
usage: Literary for light showing through a surface and, above all, for emotions betraying themselves ('dalle sue parole traspariva la delusione'); 'lasciar trasparire' means to let show. Irregular like apparire: traspaio (or trasparisco), trasparve, trasparso; takes essere.

examples.it: Dal suo sguardo traspariva una grande stanchezza.
examples.en: Great tiredness showed in his eyes.

examples.it: Non lasciò trasparire alcuna emozione durante la sentenza.
examples.en: She let no emotion show during the sentencing.

examples.it: Dalla lettera è trasparso tutto il suo rancore.
examples.en: All his resentment came through in the letter.

en: to transpose (music, a matrix); to adapt (a work to another medium); to shift
patterns: trasporre un brano in un'altra tonalità
trasporre un romanzo per il cinema
usage: Technical in music (to shift a piece into another key), mathematics (to transpose a matrix) and criticism (to adapt a novel for stage or screen, 'trasposizione cinematografica'); also to invert the order of elements. Irregular like porre: traspongo, trasposi, trasposto; future trasporrò.

examples.it: Il pianista ha trasposto il brano un tono più in basso per la cantante.
examples.en: The pianist transposed the piece a tone lower for the singer.

examples.it: Il regista traspose il romanzo ottocentesco nella Milano di oggi.
examples.en: The director transposed the nineteenth-century novel to present-day Milan.

examples.it: Se trasponiamo la matrice, le righe diventano colonne.
examples.en: If we transpose the matrix, the rows become columns.

en: to be urgent; to be urgently needed; to press
usage: In the common need sense, the urgently needed thing is the subject ('urge una riforma', 'urgono rinforzi'), or the construction is impersonal before an infinitive ('urge intervenire'). More literary uses mean to press or urge and can have personal subjects. The passato remoto, past participle and compound tenses are not used; 'urgente' is common as an adjective.

examples.it: Urge una decisione prima che la situazione peggiori.
examples.en: A decision is urgently needed before the situation gets worse.

examples.it: Urgevano rinforzi, ma il comando non rispondeva.
examples.en: Reinforcements were urgently needed, but headquarters did not reply.

examples.it: Urgerebbe un intervento del governo sui prezzi dell'energia.
examples.en: Government action on energy prices would be urgently needed.

en: to cherish (a dream, an idea); to long for, to contemplate fondly
usage: Literary verb (from 'vago' in the old sense of lovely) for dwelling lovingly on a desired image or plan, often unrealistic ('vagheggiava un ritorno alla terra'). More dreamy than 'desiderare', more nostalgic than 'sognare'; frequently ironic in journalism. Regular -are verb (vagheggio, vagheggi).

examples.it: Da giovane vagheggiava una carriera da esploratore.
examples.en: As a young man he cherished dreams of a career as an explorer.

examples.it: Alcuni vagheggiano ancora un impossibile ritorno alla lira.
examples.en: Some still fondly contemplate an impossible return to the lira.

examples.it: Vagheggiando un futuro che non sarebbe mai arrivato, lasciò passare il presente.
examples.en: Dreaming of a future that would never come, he let the present slip by.

en: to prophesy, to foretell (often ironically)
usage: Learned verb (from 'vate', the inspired poet-seer) for solemn prophecy, nearly always ironic in modern usage about pundits and economists who 'vaticinano' catastrophes. 'Predire' and 'prevedere' are neutral, 'profetizzare' religious, 'vaticinare' pompous. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Gli analisti vaticinavano il crollo della moneta unica.
examples.en: Analysts were prophesying the collapse of the single currency.

examples.it: Chi aveva vaticinato la fine del libro di carta si è dovuto ricredere.
examples.en: Those who had foretold the end of the paper book have had to think again.

examples.it: Non vaticinerei sventure prima di vedere i dati.
examples.en: I wouldn't prophesy disaster before seeing the data.

en: to harass, to oppress; to bully (with abuse of power)
usage: Formal-juridical verb for persistent ill-treatment by someone in a position of power (a tax authority, a landlord, an employer); the noun 'vessazione' and the adjective 'vessatorio' ('clausole vessatorie', unfair contract terms) are standard legal vocabulary. 'Angariare' is its more literary twin, 'tormentare' the everyday word. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: I contribuenti si sentono vessati da una burocrazia opprimente.
examples.en: Taxpayers feel harassed by an oppressive bureaucracy.

examples.it: Il caporale vessava le reclute con punizioni assurde.
examples.en: The corporal bullied the recruits with absurd punishments.

examples.it: Se continueranno a vessarci con controlli pretestuosi, ci rivolgeremo al giudice.
examples.en: If they keep harassing us with spurious inspections, we will go to court.

en: to be in force; to be in effect (of laws, rules, customs)
usage: Juridical verb used almost exclusively in the third person of simple tenses for laws, regulations or customs being in force ('vige il divieto di sosta', 'usanze che vigono ancora'). The adjective 'vigente' ('la normativa vigente') is more common than the finite forms. The subject is the rule or custom that is in force. Compound tenses are not part of ordinary use.

examples.it: In quel paese vige ancora la pena di morte.
examples.en: The death penalty is still in force in that country.

examples.it: All'epoca vigevano regole molto più severe sull'abbigliamento.
examples.en: At the time much stricter dress rules were in force.

examples.it: Finché vigerà questo regolamento, non potremo fare eccezioni.
examples.en: As long as these rules remain in force, we cannot make exceptions.
